conviction_note: Webull's own June 2026 monthly data (89.4M options contracts, 42% of all of Q2's 213M) and the CEO's August call remarks ('options steady' in July, 'August even stronger than July') point to Q3 options volume up roughly 25-30% q/q. That would put revenue at or above the top of a disputed $214-223M bar. Against that: Cboe's industry single-stock options were -8% q/q, Futu's US-stock volume was -24% q/q this morning, the analysts can see the monthly metrics on Webull's IR site (they raised estimates 17% in 3 months), and the call will be about Q4 account flows after the 7 Oct House China report, which no source covers. So the findings sum to +0.8, p_up is held at 53 because the revenue bar is disputed, abs_move is set slightly above the 8.5% straddle for a thin, retail, call-heavy name at its 52-week low, and the scaled number is +0.57.
bar: Q3 2026 EPS $0.06: Chartmill and the Yahoo two-analyst average agree. Revenue is disputed: $214.3M (wire summary), $215.6M (Yahoo avg, https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/BULL/analysis/), $216.5M (Benzinga, https://www.benzinga.com/quote/BULL/earnings-forecasts) and $222.74M (Chartmill/FXEmpire, https://www.chartmill.com/stock/quote/BULL/estimates, 'revised up 16.94% in the past 3 months'). Taken as ~$218M, range $214-223M. Webull gives no revenue guidance (Q2 release and call: none). Kalshi funded-accounts market ~5.30-5.35M (https://kalshi.com/company-reports/bull, snippet only, the page returned 429). Because the revenue bar has no company guide and its sources disagree by 4%, findings that depend on it are capped small.
positioning_check: Short interest 41.6M shares, 3.0 days to cover, settlement 2026-09-30 (massive.com https://massive.com/quote/bull; curvedtrading agrees). About 5-6% of float per equibles (undated). No November settlement found. That is not a crowded short. 25-delta skew is -15.94 vol points (calls bid over puts), put/call OI 0.17, ATM IV 141%, straddle 8.53%. The option market leans to upside and is heavy with retail calls. Tape: spot $4.63 at the 52-week low (+0.01% above it), -21.65% over 20 days, -6.65% over 5 days, -54.8% from the 52-week high, -36% since the 6 Oct close of $7.28 before the House report.

findings.finding: Webull's own June 2026 monthly release shows 89.4M options contracts (+43% m/m) and $105.8B equity notional in June alone, against Q2 totals of 213M and $279B. On the 19 Aug call the CEO said July options were 'pretty steady' with equities slightly softer than June, and 'August is looking even stronger than July'. Carried forward, that run-rate implies Q3 options of roughly 265-285M (+25-34% q/q) and equities of about $290-310B (+5-10% q/q). Q2 trading revenue was $147.7M, total $198.8M, and the bar of ~$218M implies only +8-12% q/q total revenue growth.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (19 Aug) record volumes and a beat: close 7.93 to 8.64 (+9.0%) and to 8.85 the next day (stocktwits reported +11% after hours). Q1 2026 (21 May) EPS miss: 6.99 to 6.61 (-5.4%), then 6.18. Q4 2025 (24 Mar) miss: 5.31 to 5.13 (-3.4%). Q3 2025 (20 Nov 2025) beat: 8.22 to 8.25 (+0.4%). Yahoo daily bars https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/BULL?range=1y&interval=1d
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The CFO said monthly metrics sit on the IR site, and the high estimate was revised up 17% in 3 months, so the street may already carry most of this. The Yahoo and Benzinga averages ($215-217M) look like they do not. If the run-rate were fully in the bar, every source would sit at $225M or above; they spread from $214M to $223M. Webull's July-September monthly figures could not be reached from here (the IR host does not resolve and no press-release copies were found).
findings.independence: The call commentary (https://gloom.sh/stocks/bull/transcripts/q2-2026, 2026-08-19) and the monthly table are both company sources, so this is one finding. Robinhood's Q3 (finding 2) is a separate peer source pointing the same way.

findings.finding: Robinhood's Q3 2026 (reported 27 Oct, after Webull last spoke) had record options contracts of 905M, up 17% q/q from 774M in Q2, and equity notional of $992B, up 4% q/q from $956B. Options revenue rose from $342M to $399M (+17% q/q), net interest revenue +7% q/q, margin book a record $22.1B. Crypto revenue fell 55% y/y, which barely touches Webull (crypto was about $2.25M, ~1% of its Q2 revenue).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: BULL rose with the brokerage group on 9 Nov (+3%, with HOOD +4%) per 247wallst. No measured BULL reaction to HOOD prints.
findings.why_not_priced: It is public for three weeks, so analysts have probably used it, and BULL fell 20% over 20 days anyway because of the China overhang. What it adds is that the closest US retail peer gained share in single-stock options while the industry shrank (finding 3), which supports the high end of the bar rather than the low.
findings.independence: A peer print (Q2 releases https://finviz.com/news/374402/robinhood-reports-second-quarter-2026-results for the q/q base). It is independent of Webull's own data but is a peer, not a counterparty.

findings.finding: Cboe's Q3 2026 industry review: market-wide options ADV of 70.6M was 4% below Q2's record, single-stock options ADV fell 8% q/q to 32.7M, and retail order flow was 'slower' in July and August after the June spike from the end of the PDT rule, before reaching an all-time high in September.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measured for industry series on BULL.
findings.source_date: 2026-10 (Q3 2026 review; month read from the page, exact day not shown)
findings.why_not_priced: It is an industry proxy that cuts against the company's own June exit rate and HOOD's +17%. It matters if Webull's mix behaves like the industry's single-stock options and not like HOOD's. A market that priced it would hold the bar near $214M, which some sources do.
findings.independence: Independent of findings 1 and 2. Futu (finding 4) points the same way but has a different customer base.

findings.finding: Futu reported Q3 2026 before the US open today (19 Nov). US-stock trading volume was HK$3.81T, down 24.0% q/q; total volume -22.0% q/q; revenue -7.1% q/q; the blended commission rate fell from 7.5bps to 5.6bps. Funded accounts rose 4.2% q/q.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured BULL reaction to Futu prints. Peer co-movement: BULL and FUTU are both down 35-38% year to date (247wallst 9 Nov).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it came out before the 18:08 UTC seal, and BULL is down about 0.5% today to its 52-week low. Futu's clients are mostly Asian investors trading US stocks. Webull is about 89% US revenue (247wallst) with ~810K international funded accounts, so the read-through is weak.
findings.independence: Separate filer. It agrees in direction with the Cboe industry series (finding 3).

findings.finding: The House Select Committee on China's 7 Oct report ('Free Trades, Hidden Ties') sent the stock from $7.28 to $5.89 that day. The committee followed up on 20 Oct, accusing Webull of 'numerous false statements', and the panel questioned its data-security assurances on 27 Oct. Q4-to-date funded accounts, net deposits and account closures since the report will be disclosed for the first time on this call; no October Webull metric was found. Industry October was flat: HOOD equity +1% and options flat m/m, IBKR DARTs +5% m/m.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 7 Oct report day: -19% (7.28 to 5.89). No prior print has carried Q4-to-date flow commentary under a regulatory overhang.
findings.why_not_priced: The direction is genuinely unknown. The stock is already 36% below its pre-report close, so the price assumes a lot of damage. If management shows October deposits and account openings held up, that would remove some of the overhang. If closures or outflows show up, it confirms the bear case. Nobody outside the company has an October Webull number (the Kalshi page and the IR site were unreachable).
findings.independence: Industry October data: https://finviz.com/news/422249/robinhood-markets-inc-reports-october-2026-operating-data (HOOD, 2026-11-12) and https://fxnewsgroup.com/forex-news/retail-forex/interactive-brokers-registers-4-y-y-decrease-in-darts-in-october-2026/ (IBKR). Both are peers and say nothing about Webull's own flows.

findings.finding: On 5 Nov FINRA fined Webull Financial $4.2M for AML, identity-theft-prevention and best-execution failures (more than 120,000 accounts approved without a reasonable basis to believe the identities were genuine), and required it to hire an independent consultant. A securities class action covering purchases from 26 Apr 2025 to 6 Oct 2026 is pending.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: A separate $1.6M FINRA fine in 2025 had no measured reaction.
findings.why_not_priced: The fine is public and small against Q2 adjusted operating profit of $62.6M. It matters only if the consultant requirement slows onboarding or if legal accruals appear in Q3 or Q4 opex.
findings.independence: Shares the regulatory-overhang theme with finding 5 but is a different fact.

findings.finding: Webull has a $100M buyback authorisation and used only about $11M of it in Q2 (1,820,788 shares at an average $6.03). It held $701.6M of cash at 30 June, with the $200M revolver undrawn. The stock now trades at $4.63, 23% below the Q2 average repurchase price, so accelerated buybacks or a larger authorisation are a plausible announcement on this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buyback was disclosed with the Q2 print, which rose about 9%, so the effect cannot be separated from the beat.
findings.why_not_priced: This is an inference about what management will do, not a disclosed plan. If the market expected a bigger buyback, the stock would probably not be sitting at its low with about $89M of authorisation unused. Q3 buyback activity is only disclosed with the print.
findings.independence: Cash and facility figures: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001866364/000121390026099290/ea030409301ex99-2.htm (the same company's Q2 MD&A). Same issuer, so not independent.

findings.finding: The CFO guided H2 2026 marketing spend to be 'similar in quantum to the first half', no lower than Q2's $35.0M and no higher than Q1's $49.4M, while adjusted opex grows with brokerage and transaction costs. Q2's 31.5% adjusted operating margin came at the bottom of that marketing range, so a Q3 move toward Q1's level is inside guidance but would compress margin.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q1 2026 EPS miss came with marketing at $49.4M and sold -5.4%. Q2 at $35.0M paired with a +9% move.
findings.why_not_priced: It sits inside what the company guided, so its size is near zero. It matters for the EPS bar of $0.06, which is above Q2's GAAP diluted EPS of $0.04.
findings.independence: The marketing figures come from the Q2 MD&A 6-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001866364/000121390026099290/ea030409301ex99-2.htm), the same issuer.

findings.finding: New product lines are scaling: prediction-markets revenue was about $5-6M in Q2, up 71% q/q (call), and HOOD event contracts kept growing (October 5.9B, +136% y/y). Extended-hours single-stock options (announced 22 Oct) and US perpetual futures from November give management new Q4 talking points.
findings.why_not_priced: These are small against $200M+ quarterly revenue and the launches are public. They matter only if management quantifies early uptake.
findings.independence: Q2 prediction-market figure: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/webull-q2-earnings-call-highlights (secondary report of the call).

findings.finding: Positioning into the print is lopsided toward retail upside: put/call OI 0.17, 25-delta skew -15.9 (calls bid), a 52-week low, -21.7% over 20 days. Short interest of 41.6M shares is 3.0 days to cover (30 Sep). Supply overhang from September: the President sold 53,846 shares at about $9.58 (Form 4, 8 Sep) and an F-3 (1 Sep) registered resale of Pi Securities acquisition shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q2 beat, from a depressed level, moved +9%.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is the price itself, so this is mostly priced. It is filed so the judges see that the short is not crowded and that the call-heavy book may amplify a relief move or punish a miss.

baseline_tension: The small positive lean agrees with the call-bid skew (-15.9) and cuts against the -21.7% 20-day run-up and the 52-week low, which carry the China overhang rather than any quarterly fundamental. A positive sign does not need to beat the skew; it needs the Q4-flow commentary not to confirm the overhang, and that is unknowable from outside.
lessons_applied: Rule 6, disputed bar: revenue consensus ranges $214-223M with no company guide, so the bar-dependent findings were capped. Finding 1 went from 1.0 to 0.7 and finding 2 from 0.5 to 0.4; p_up went from 54 to 53.
Rule 5, proxy vs company number: the Cboe industry proxy was trimmed from -0.5 to -0.4. It stays below the company's own June exit rate in size.

Rule 5, 'drawdown is not a cause' and Rule 3, own caveat: the Q4-flow/China finding was sized +0.3 on the argument that a -36% drawdown has priced the damage. It is now -0.2, because the direction is unknown and the committee kept pressing on 20 and 27 Oct.
Rule 2, one-off: the FINRA fine was cut from -0.2 to -0.1. It is $4.2M against $62.6M quarterly adjusted operating profit.

Rule 7, positioning: the short is not crowded (3.0 DTC), so the negatives were not shrunk for squeeze risk. The September insider and F-3 supply facts were merged into the positioning finding, which went from +0.3 to +0.2.

Rule 1 and Rule 8: the reaction history (+9% on the Q2 beat, -5.4% on the Q1 miss) shows this name pays for the line, and coverage is thin (two or three analysts). abs_move was kept at 9.5, above the 8.53% straddle.
